title: caching Redis invalidation eviction and stampede
concepts: A cache keeps a faster or closer copy of data to reduce repeated work; it is an optimization whose correctness depends on an explicit freshness, invalidation, and failure policy.

Cache-aside loads on demand: read cache, load the source on a miss, populate cache, and invalidate or refresh after source writes. It is simple and naturally bounds cached data to the working set, but permits stale windows and concurrent miss amplification.

TTL expiration bounds an entry's lifetime but does not itself ensure freshness before expiry. Invalidation after a write reduces stale duration but creates ordering and failure windows; use versions, write-through, or an explicit staleness budget where required.

Memory pressure requires a deliberate eviction policy. Redis distinguishes all-key and expiring-key candidate sets, LRU recency, LFU frequency, LRM modification time, random selection, TTL-based choice, and no-eviction rejection; cache data must tolerate eviction.

A cache stampede occurs when concurrent requests regenerate a missing or expired hot key together. Single-flight coordination, a short-lived lock, stale-while-revalidate, TTL jitter, or probabilistic early refresh can reduce origin load, each with its own stale-data and coordination tradeoffs.

Redis is a data-structure server as well as a cache. Choose a native data type for the access pattern, but do not assume in-memory data is automatically durable, non-evictable, or equivalent to the authoritative database.

items: Redis transaction does not support rollback
Redis 8.6 adds LRM (Least Recently Modified) eviction policies: allkeys-lrm and volatile-lrm. LRM ages keys by last modification rather than reads; these are distinct from older LRU and LFU policies.
SET adds IFEQ, IFNE, IFDEQ, and IFDNE conditional update options; DELEX adds compare-and-delete, and MSETEX adds atomic multi-key setting with a shared expiration.
INCREX atomically increments a numeric string key and sets its expiration, combining counter update and TTL assignment in one command.
Streams add XACKDEL and XDELEX, and XADD/XTRIM gain KEEPREF, DELREF, and ACKED options to control how trimming and deletion interact with pending consumer-group references.
Redis Functions provide managed server-side programmability as an alternative to volatile application-loaded EVAL scripts.

Database-specific cache coherence, database query design, and EF Core caching APIs (tracks 03 and 04)

Do not imply that Redis is always volatile or cannot persist data; durability depends on deployment and persistence configuration, while this manifest focuses on cache semantics and Redis data structures

Redis Open Source command inventory is bounded to cache/keyspace/data-type/eviction/programmability surfaces named here; this is not a complete inventory of every Redis command or optional module command
